blocks.text: Пока is used as an adverb of time and as a conjunction. Пока не (until) is a conjunction. A. The adverb of time — пока — means: 1) *Никому не говорите об этом пока!* — for the time being; 2) *Сведений о самолёте пока (ещё) нет.* — as yet; 3) *Я посижу здесь, а ты пока сбегай в лавку.* — in the meantime.

B. The conjunction ПОКА — while — introduces adverbial clauses of time. The action of both the main and the subordinate clauses can: a) completely coincide in time (imperfective verbs are used in both): *Пока шёл дождь, мы стояли под деревом.* b) partly coincide in time (perfective aspect is used in one of the clauses or in both): *Пока она готовила обед, я написал 2 письма.*

C. The construction ПОКА НЕ (until, before) is used as a unit to introduce subordinate adverbial clauses of time. ПОКА НЕ has no negative meaning and the particle НЕ is not translated: *Он читал, пока не устали глаза. Я посижу здесь, пока вы не придёте.* Sometimes a compound conjunction — ДО ТЕХ ПОР ПОКА НЕ — is used instead: *Ученик повторял адрес до тех пор, пока не выучил его наизусть.*
From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 105.

The exercises are real sentences: from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR), with their English translations, and from the public-domain Russian books in this library, with author and title. The word in brackets is the dictionary form of the missing word.
